items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: pick out a hero, pick out somebody you really want to emulate or a couple of guys you really want to emulate. Whether it’s Bernard Purdie or Al Jackson or Roger Hawkins

ctx.x: Well in my mind and in my ears the young musician today has so many more advantages than I had in terms of what’s available for research purposes between YouTube and all the recordings and all the different formats and all the different places they can see somebody that they want to emulate, or listen to something, download it, stream it, and practice with it 24 hours a day to get that feel, and I hear a lot of good young drummers who have done exactly that: downloaded the records, a lot of them, especially the…

what’s on the record, this is what I’ve got to play, and I’ve got to figure out a way to get that sound you know whether it means tuning the snare drum way, way high and putting a pot lid on it so it’s got this metallic backbeat to it, metallic sound, or putting a piece of construction material on it like these aluminum 2 X 4 sections that they use instead of 2 X 4s these days. You compress that and it’s a great metallic snare drum sound. I’ve used that a couple of times. And ridiculous little tiny electronic…
